teaser: Founders, customers and investors are each protected from the others because anyone can fork; forks take hold only after a breakdown.
core_idea: In an open source company every corner of the triangle of founders, customers and investors has an exit that takes the technology with it, and each exit has a condition: founders need no broad non-compete, customers need their data to move, investors need to afford a team. Forking is a last resort and the famous forks that took hold followed a breakdown; where the original kept executing, the fork stayed a hedge. A maturing company can move a shared component to a neutral home and let its explorers carry on with the code.

figures.caption: Three corners, one exit each: the open code sits in the middle, and each corner can take it and carry on. The founders can leave if no broad non-compete stops them; the investors can fund a team next door if they can pay for it; the customers can move if their data leaves with them, cheaply. Illustrative.

Six forks: what broke, the year each fork began, and what happened next. MariaDB stayed a hedge while MySQL kept shipping; io.js merged back once a foundation fixed the governance; LibreOffice, Nextcloud, OpenTofu and Valkey took hold after a new owner, a change of direction or a licence change.

Commits a year to the trunk branch of mysql/mysql-server: about 8,900 in 2019 and about 2,800 in 2025, a fall of roughly two thirds. 2026 runs to 28 September. Measured by this site from a clone of the repository.
